Use only the tools exposed for this stage. Use read_documents to batch several needed pages in one call, avoiding repeated model round-trips. Use the supplied stage-scoped catalog; do not read arbitrary paths or earlier runs. The originating study and its explanations remain hidden. For case units, definitions or processing facts, use request_case_definition; an isolated service releases only reviewed neutral facts with opaque evidence IDs. General literature retrieval remains restricted to independently dated earlier sources. You may reason conditionally while a case fact remains unknown. Use search_sources for actual missing public knowledge; returned access depth is explicit, not proof of relevance. analyze_csv reads every selected row, not the 12-row preview. Submit once using submit_result; if validation fails, the draft is saved locally. Use patch_result with the latest draft_ref and only changed fields; do not regenerate unchanged text. Original submissions remain archived. Every result requires summary (nonempty string) and artifacts, evidence, claims, limitations, next_actions (arrays, empty allowed), plus stage-specific fields. For development_step focus/uptake source, use a supplied source ID, document ID or unambiguous registered filename. Use a source-field locator instead of copying an exact quote when convenient. A registered document ID/path suffices if no specific field is selected; optional paraphrases are stored separately from exact quotes. For a JSON source, quote the exact string VALUE, without adding its field name. Alternatively supply quote_pointer (JSON pointer to a string) and omit quote; the exact selected string will be resolved and logged. For learning_request, context_ref="development_step" may replace duplicate gap/why_now strings; this references your own gap/reason, never changes its content. For sources[].local_path use the returned D-document ID to avoid copying long paths; it resolves to the exact registered file. source_use covers exactly broker_reply_source_ids, not the whole source catalog or new searches in this turn. Cite newly read tool sources in evidence/memory_notes with actual paths/URLs. Keep result text concise; use 0-1 useful memory notes unless multiple are necessary. Preserve branches and open issues. files is an object of relative artifact paths to complete text content; every declared artifact must exist or be provided in files. If artifacts is empty, your exact summary is saved automatically as an artifact; do not repeat the entire JSON as prose. For review-index-v2, start with the stage directory and read relevant result/before-input sections by document ID. Summaries are incomplete navigation excerpts, not evidence. Start with input_refs and inline bodies, not the entire provenance catalog. When reading a needed document, request the relevant JSON pointer or a useful page (up to 12000 characters); avoid repeated tiny probes. For review, source_stage must match the stage containing the exact quote; note_keys are actual memory_notes keys (often empty), not JSON field names. If an input body is omitted or represented by $document, read it by ID. No scientific text was summarized; originals and before-inputs remain readable. Online retrieval is enabled.

Execute agent_learn.md's learning and co-questioning plan. Chinese readable artifacts.
Do not read earlier project runs/candidates. Only use listed inputs, their cited source files,
the current case's exchanges, supplied memory, and public sources. A previous task is accessible
only through the supplied memory packet and its provenance. Do not scan old run directories.
Read the actual common sources behind summaries. Treat published findings as published knowledge.
Do not present them as discoveries. Preserve disagreements and all idea branches.
Use public sources via urllib/curl (Crossref, Europe PMC, PMC, arXiv, publishers as accessible).
Save retrieved text and exact URLs; distinguish full text, abstract and failed access.
No solving, scientific validation experiment, proof or novelty gate is required for ideas.
Small worked calculations are allowed to learn a concept, clearly labelled learning examples.
Save result.json with the six runtime fields plus the requested fields. Use summary as a STRING.
Do not spend your entire budget retrieving; save useful partial understanding if needed.
Study your actual controller reply. Identify directly relevant sources, transferable methods and irrelevant results; explain what changes in your assumption and what remains open. Classify every returned source; not_read is valid for sources not studied. Return source_use:[{source_id,relation:direct/method/irrelevant/not_read,reason}], learning_change, and an optional next learning_request. Label hypothetical worked examples. 
Also return memory_notes: 0-3 reusable notes; [] when unchanged. Each object has:
key (stable lower_case ASCII concept key; reuse an existing key when correcting it), title,
kind (source_knowledge/interpretation/hypothesis/correction),
mastery (read/explained/used; identify how the knowledge informed actual research when used),
understanding, conditions, open_questions (nonempty strings), optional example (text or null),
tags (array, include English and Chinese terms), sources (array of actual URLs or source paths),
revision_reason (required when the key already exists).
Separate published knowledge, your inference and untested hypotheses. 'Unknown' is a valid
open_questions string, never invent competence. Describe corrections explicitly.
Also return memory_use: array of {key,source_task,used_for,scope_check} for notes actually used;
return [] if none. State what you still cannot explain/use.


HYPOTHESIS DEVELOPMENT v3:
Use your disciplinary understanding and screened long-term memory to develop assumptions.
Start from a specific phenomenon, tension, difficulty or missing relation. When you have a
possible explanation or organizing principle, state what you suppose; merely changing a
'whether' question into an affirmative sentence adds no insight. An assumption can be an
explanation, conjectured relation, representation, distinction or method/construction principle.
Explore what conceptual move it makes and, CONDITIONALLY on the assumption, what changes in
our understanding or possible actions. Develop concrete consequences, not promises of impact.
Use these as thinking moves, not a checklist that every early idea must already satisfy.
Before requesting learning, identify a specific missing conceptual connection in the current
assumption, why it matters, and what understanding might change. Return to that same gap after
reading: explain a revised premise, relation or conditional consequence, or retain the gap.
Do not substitute more citations, caveats, controls or formal wording for conceptual development.
Measurement/method contributions remain valid when their concrete intellectual consequences are
articulated. No compulsory mechanism, scientific breakthrough, or progress at each turn.

In peer discussion, engage a specific assumption: elaborate a consequence, expose a hidden
premise, connect a disciplinary concept, propose a distinct explanation, or revise a relation.
Explain the reasoning. You may retain, revise, branch, or park your own line. No forced consensus,
disagreement, novelty claim, completed hypothesis or compulsory new branch each turn.
Evidence strength, proof, available data/tools, implementation and experimental feasibility
are NOT requirements for proposing, retaining or prioritizing a hypothesis. Do not turn
discussion into a feasibility review. Research/analysis requests remain optional resources
for thinking. Correct concrete errors in premises while keeping conditional hypotheses distinct
from established observations; lack of evidence alone is not a refutation.

hypothesis_state.self contains your saved branches; peer_branches belong to their named owners.
Return hypothesis_updates: [] when nothing changed, otherwise full cards:
{key: stable local identifier [A-Za-z0-9_]+, base_version: 0 for new or supplied own version,
assumption: nonempty provisional claim, motivation: specific phenomenon/difficulty/relation,
conceptual_move: string or null if still unclear,
implications: [specific conditional consequences, may be empty],
open_questions: [unresolved conceptual questions, may be empty],
status: developing/parked, reason: why propose/change/park/resume,
influenced_by: [exact ref objects from supplied hypothesis_state],
depends_on: [exact supplied hypothesis refs used as premises; [] if none]}.
Influence is not logical dependence. Declare depends_on only for actual premises; do not invent
links. revision_obligations lists your branches whose declared premises changed or themselves
await review. This does NOT mean the branch is false. For each obligation return
 dependency_responses:[{ref:exact hypothesis_ref,action:revise/reaffirm/park/unresolved,reason}].
Reaffirm/revise requires an updated full card citing current dependency versions; changing only
links is recorded as provenance maintenance, not conceptual progress. Park/unresolved retains
the branch and its warning. Reasoned reaffirmation is valid; do not mechanically follow criticism.
Dependencies not explicitly declared cannot be inferred by this structural checker.
Omitting a branch retains it. To keep an alternative, use a new key and cite the parent ref;
never overwrite a peer's branch. Missing conceptual_move or implications is allowed for an
early assumption. Keep hypothetical consequences explicitly hypothetical, including examples.
Reusable conceptual learning can also be saved through existing memory_notes, kind:hypothesis,
with actual source provenance and same-key revisions. Run-local branches do not replace your
long-term disciplinary memory or its source screening. Do not invent empirical support.


Optional learning_request: {needed:boolean, gap, why_now, queries:[strings],
urls:[], source_ids:[], record_ids:[], operations:[], case_questions:[]}.
Use case_questions for actual case definitions/units/processing order; literature cannot
reconstruct undocumented case facts. These questions dispatch even when needed:false.
General theory and explanation-development requests use queries/gap. For case facts, the
isolated material service releases supported neutral definitions, not hidden conclusions.
The controller searches and returns actual readable content. Keep your own scientific query;
classify returned sources as directly relevant, transferable method, or irrelevant, with reasons.
Do not treat a successful download as understanding. No compulsory tool use.
For a small worked calculation use an operation {kind:"calculation", question,
bindings:{name: numeric scalar/array}, expression: numeric array expression,
expected: optional numeric value/array}. Available arithmetic, slices and named functions
include mean,sum,std,norm,diff,abs,sqrt. Define which rows/columns mean which entities.
Top-level analysis_plan also dispatches. needed:false disables literature search, not explicit
calculations. Unsupported requests return a pending capability task; no scientific rejection.
Keep purely tentative proposals in hypothesis_updates/next_actions, not execution fields.


HYPOTHESIS CONTENT CYCLE:
Use development_cycle as a thinking context, not a demand to invent progress. Choose one
specific explanatory relation, construction, distinction or unresolved phenomenon from its
sources. Locate the conceptual gap: what connection/premise/consequence is still unclear?
Choose a next move because of this gap: learn, derive, connect, reframe, or hold. Explain why
that move could change understanding. For learning, use this gap in learning_request.gap and
why_now, and formulate targeted queries; do not request a broad survey merely to fill a stage.
In discussion, take up a peer's concrete relation and explain how your discipline extends,
challenges or changes its consequences. Generic agreement about controls or feasibility is
not a substitute; a measurement contribution is valid when its specific consequences matter.
Study returned services against the gap that requested them, including failures and pending
capabilities. Do not call retrieval success learning. If nothing changes, say so and preserve
the gap. Own previous_steps carry unfinished thinking across phases and sessions. When the
controller flags repeated_no_change, reconsider the missing connection, premise, or next
learning move; holding a branch is valid. The flag uses supplied peer content comparisons, not a quality verdict. A shared interpretation is normal.
Return development_step:{focus:{source:exact development_cycle.sources key,quote:exact excerpt},
gap:nonempty text, action:learn/derive/connect/reframe/hold, reason:nonempty text,
expected_change:text or null for hold,
uptake:[{source:exact source key,quote:exact excerpt or null only for unresolved,
effect:revise/extend/challenge/unchanged/unresolved,reason:how this affects the focus,
consequence:conditional consequence or null when none follows}],
outcome:{kind:relation/implication/clarification/unchanged/uncertain,
statement:what changed or did not, remaining_gap:text or null}}.
Account once for EACH service key in required_service_uptake. If peer_sources is nonempty,
engage at least one (unresolved with a reason is valid). Other uptake is optional. Quotes must
come from the named source; for published claims quote readable source content, not metadata.
For relation/implication outcomes, preserve the resulting claim in a hypothesis_update's
assumption or implications. This records an author's proposal, NOT confirmed novelty/progress.
No compulsory new relation, branch, agreement, data, experiment, proof or implementation.


QUESTION STATE PROTOCOL v2:
question_state.self is YOUR authoritative current personal question. peer_questions belong
to their named owners. shared_question is the discussion's current shared question, or null.
Do not reconstruct your prior question from the latest peer message. The controller records
the actual before-state; do NOT return question_before or question_after.
Return personal_question_update: {base: the exact self.ref object, action: retain/revise,
question: your current or revised personal question, reason: a nonempty explanation,
influenced_by: array of exact question ref objects from this supplied packet}.
Retain means the question text stays exactly the same. Revise may include adopting a peer's
line or the shared question: explain why; use influenced_by to identify relevant question refs.
You need not preserve disagreement or a distinct personal question if you decide to change it.
Separately return shared_question_update: null, or {base: the exact shared_question.ref (null
if none yet), action: propose/revise/retain, question: shared question text, reason: nonempty,
influenced_by: array of refs from this packet}. Propose is only for a first shared question.
A shared question is a versioned proposal, not proof of peer agreement. Revising it NEVER
changes another researcher's personal question. Your own personal update is independent too.

Use controller-owned question_state, never invent question_before/question_after.
Keep hypotheses tied to specific entities/relations in this situation. A measurement or representation contribution is legitimate; explain its concrete consequences without forcing a natural mechanism.

and Control of Magnetic Shape Memory Alloy Actuators.\",\"date\":\"2022-06-22\",\"publication_dates\":[\"2022-06-22\",\"2022-06-22\"],\"doi\":\"https://doi.org/10.3390/ma15134400\",\"url\":\"https://doi.org/10.3390/ma15134400\",\"text\":\"In the last three decades, the number of investigations focusing on the application of a new type of drive system known as unconventional, smart, or even intelligent has increased significantly, typically with the aim of meeting new engineering requirements such as better dynamic performance, an increase in the power to weight ratio, weight reduction, and the improvement of positioning accuracy and durability. New, advanced drives are especially in demand for use in high precision positioning devices, special machines, precise manipulators, medicinal devices and military equipment [ 1 ], with their construction frequently involving the use of so-called smart materials to replace complex mechanical structures such as torque motors in servo valves. Studies examining the development of new actuators based on smart materials have been undertaken at both academic institutions [ 2 , 3 ] and companies, e.g., ETO Group [ 4 ].\\nSmart materials are now most commonly used as drive elements. For example, piezoelectric crystals have been employed in engineering applications since the mid-19th century and are currently used in high-precision actuators, such as those of atomic force microscopes [ 5 ]. Such crystals are distinguished by their high dynamic bandwidth, sub-nanometre resolution and very short response times, making them suitable for fast and very accurate positioning tasks. One interesting application of piezo elements is their use in pneumatic or hydraulic servo-valves, where a very precise torque motor is replaced by piezo stacks [ 6 , 7 ] or piezo bender actuators [ 8 , 9 ]. Other smart materials used today in precise drives may be magnetically active, including magnetostrictive materials such as Terfenol-D. Although both piezo and magnetostrictive elements are characterised by their high dynamics, they exhibit rather weak deformation of not more than tens of micrometres [ 10 , 11 ]. Shape memory alloys (SMAs), initially developed in the mid-20th century, are currently attracting increased attention in a wide range of disciplines as a competitive alternative to other non-classical actuators. The main distinguishing feature of SMAs is their large deformation in comparison to other groups of smart materials. Unfortunately, the dynamics of thermally activated SMAs (TSMAs) is very weak, particularly during the cooling phase, with time constants of step responses equal to a few seconds [ 12 , 13 ]. Nevertheless, interesting applications of TSMAs include their use in bi-stable safety valves, which open automatically with a rise in ambient temperature (thermostat mode). In such instruments the TSMA wires work without an electronic control system, acting as a safety valve [ 14 ]. The design and nonlinear control of beam-like structural deflection by TSMA wires is presented in papers [ 12 , 15 , 16 ]. Technical analysis of the practical application of SMA structures is presented in paper [ 2 ], which provides a review of recent research and the commercial application of SMAs, including one hundred patents categorised against relevant commercial domains and rated with respect to relevant design objectives.\\nOne special group of SMAs are the magnetic shape memory alloys (MSMAs), active materials that change properties such as their shape and relative magnetic permeability in the presence of an external magnetic field, generating force and repeatable strains of up to 6%. The first mention of crystal lattice reorientation was published by Ullakko in 1996 [ 17 , 18 ]. The main motivation behind the design of MSMA-based actuators is to fill the gap between actuators based on TSMAs and those built of magnetostrictive materials, combining the strain scope of the former and a dynamic response expressed in milliseconds comparable to that of the latter [ 19 ].\\nAs every application of MSMAs requires the generation of a magnetic field, the key element in MSMA-based drives is the magnetic circuit and a coil, the design of which is very important. Although the German company ETO Magnetic reported [ 20 ] that excitation by large currents provided very satisfying results (short response times), but the high current density in the coil increased the temperature of the actuator, which represents a considerable disadvantage because MSMAs are very sensitive to temperature changes [ 21 ]. In contrast to conventional heat-driven shape memory alloys, MSMAs exhibit higher operating frequencies, making them attractive for many actuation applications. Indeed, such properties are highly promising regarding the use of MSMAs in low displacement positioning devices. Practically, MSMAs are currently the only smart material offering the possibility of generating strains of up to 1000 µm with dynamics significantly better than that of TSMAs. To obtain a strain of about 100 µm, actuators constructed of piezo or magnetostrictive materials require mechanical amplification, for example by a complex lever system. Such a solution complicates the structure of the actuator, and reduces both its accuracy and dynamics. Mechanical amplification also provides a relatively small increase in strain, for example the strain of the actuator presented in [ 6 ] was increased only three-fold (from 30 µm to 90 µm).\\nMost actuators based on smart materials are as yet not commercial products due to their nonlinear behaviour, which makes it difficult to regulate position via open and closed loop control. The most important of these characteristics is hysteresis, which significantly influences positioning accuracy and thus many efforts have been made to overcome this problem. One of the most popular strategies involves initial hysteresis modelling, then inversing the model and finally applying it as the compensator in an open or closed loop control system [ 12 , 22 ]. Although it is possible to control an actuator with hysteresis via a closed-loop system without hysteresis compensation, this method is much more difficult and can cause drive inaccuracy and instability, with the actuator also tending to fall into oscillatory behaviour [ 23 ].\\nThe modelling of hysteresis strongly depends on its shape (with or without saturation, symmetrical or not-symmetrical, sharp); for example, the model used for the compensation","next_offset":6500,"total_characters":43507,"raw_original":false},{"ref":"D258ac2dfad1c5ae4e9c1","sha256":"258ac2dfad1c5ae4e9c1ff4a66ca57863148a48840f99157323ff518cd7840c0","pointer":"/sources/2","offset":0,"text":"{\"title\":\"Mechanical annealing and memories in a disordered solid.\",\"date\":\"2022-10-05\",\"publication_dates\":[\"2022-10-05\",\"2022-10-05\"],\"doi\":\"https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abo1614\",\"url\":\"https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abo1614\",\"text\":\"The steps to prepare a solid material for use typically go far beyond forming its chemical constituents into a desired shape. Techniques such as quenching (i.e., rapid cooling) or thermal annealing (slow, staged cooling) and mechanical deformation can markedly affect the final microscopic structure, for example, to increase hardness or strength ( 1 ). Mechanical methods show particular promise for varying the properties and broadening the applications of amorphous or disordered solids. These materials consist of atoms, particles, drops, or bubbles with negligible long-range order ( Fig. 1A ), placing them far from any ground state and ensuring a strong dependence on history. For example, despite desirable properties such as corrosion resistance and large strains before failure, bulk metallic glasses tend to start life as brittle materials that fail catastrophically ( 2 ,  3 ) but can be made less or even more brittle through deformation ( 4 ). Likewise, when studying or using the kinds of foams, concentrated suspensions, or concentrated emulsions found in consumer products or pharmaceuticals, one wishes to erase, or exploit, the effects of prior handling on rheology and microscopic structure ( 5 – 7 ).\\n( A ) 2D disordered solid, made of particles at oil-water interface with electrostatic repulsion. Arrows show displacements (exaggerated 10×) at typical “soft spot” where particles rearrange under horizontal shear. Arrow colors represent direction. ( B ) Constant-amplitude shear strain (γ) protocol: After large-amplitude reset, 176 cycles anneal material and form memory of strain amplitude. Readout (blue shaded region) tests whether the annealed state (red star) can be restored by comparing it with the states after cycles of increasing amplitude γ read  (blue dots). ( C ) Ring-down annealing is followed optionally by writing of a memory (red shaded region) and then readout. ( D  and  E ) MSD of particles, normalized by particle spacing  a , measured during readout as γ read  is increased. For each protocol, dips reveal written memories of 3 or 4% by restoring the prereadout states. Vertical dashed lines mark expected memory values. No-write curve in (E) represents no added memories and is possible only with ring-down. Error bars represent SDs of mean for multiple trials. Constant-amplitude data are from experiments in ( 26 ).\\nExperiments and simulations that cyclically shear disordered solids have illuminated this mechanical history dependence, aspects of which seem to be common to two-dimensional (2D) and 3D disordered solids with many kinds of microscopic physics ( 4 ,  8 – 15 ). In particular, athermal simulations show that when the material starts in a higher-energy configuration, as if quenched from a high-temperature liquid, and the amplitude of shear is below a critical value, this mechanical annealing lowers the overall energy of the structure ( 4 ,  9 ,  12 ,  16 – 22 ). Eventually, the material reaches a steady state in which the plastic rearrangements ( Fig. 1A ) are fully reversible; the rearrangements become periodic, and the particle trajectories become closed loops ( 9 ,  11 ,  13 ,  23 ,  24 ). Since deformation can access a vast set of metastable arrangements of particles in these glassy materials, one might imagine that this precisely periodic behavior can be sustained only by driving at constant amplitude. Reducing the amplitude of shear strain γ 0  for even one cycle generally leaves the particles in different positions. However, these mechanically annealed solids have an additional, unexpected property: Resuming the previous amplitude restores the positions and the dynamics nearly perfectly ( 25 – 28 ).\\nThis kind of stability under amplitude variation lets us see that annealing has formed a memory: Without knowing its past, one can probe a sample to reveal the strain amplitude γ a  that was used to anneal it ( 14 ,  25 ,  26 ,  29 ). We show this in  Fig. 1 (B and D)  with experiments on the 2D disordered solid from  Fig. 1A . We apply a series of cycles with increasing amplitude γ read , starting with a small value and ending past γ a  ( Fig. 1B ). At the end of each readout cycle, the positions of the particles are compared with those at the end of annealing; in  Fig. 1D , this is done with the mean squared displacement (MSD), normalized by the typical spacing between particles  a  squared. At small γ read , this displacement grows, but it drops near γ read  = γ a  when the annealed state of the system is recovered. This observation and others approximate a generic behavior called return point memory ( 30 – 32 ) that seems to be a property of annealed samples ( 26 – 28 ). The material’s tendency to retain readable memories, similar to many systems that do not relax to equilibrium ( 32 ), represents an opportunity for programming, adaptation, and diagnostics but a challenge for annealing. If annealing is meant to relax a material and ultimately lower the entropy of its structure, this outcome would seem to involve as few discernible memories of the past as possible. Could we better understand mechanical annealing if we set out to prepare a blank slate?\\nIn the experiments described here, we prepare a disordered solid with a “ring-down” proto","next_offset":5500,"total_characters":50619,"raw_original":false}],"paging":"Large batches are paginated automatically; follow next_offset for remaining text.","tool_record_ref":"Df396f571fda5090f25db","tool_record_path":"/Applications/ideas/research/hysteron_deepseek_20261110/runtime/ours_source/runs/hypothesis_development_hysteron_generation/stages/02_initial_1_learn_0/api_v2/workspace/tools/c7f7d7f4005bde1891e380d1afd12699c5929195090112dfab092886fcad0703.json"}

( 2 ) are remarkable, since they demonstrate in an explicit and experimentally accessible manner how memory can emerge in everyday systems such as a crumpled sheet of paper, thereby contributing toward our understanding of memory formation in driven disordered systems.\\nMemory-recording mechanical devices can be constructed from bistable elements ( 3 ) such as origami bellows ( 4 ), corrugated elastic sheets ( 5 ), and, more generally, mechanical metamaterials ( 6 ). Under a compression, a bistable element remains in one of its stable states, call it “0,” until the force rises above a threshold level  F + , upon which a fast relaxation snap event causes a transition into the other state, “1,” as shown in  Fig. 1  A ,  Top Left . Subsequently reducing the forcing, a transition back into state “0” will occur when the force falls below a threshold level  F − . Hysteresis emerges when the two switching fields  F ±  are such that  F − < F + , so that for values between these two thresholds the actual state of the bistable element depends on the history of the forcing. Such elementary units of hysteresis are called Preisach hysterons ( 7 – 9 ).\\n( A ,  Top Left ) Elementary hysteresis cycle of a Preisach hysteron resulting from a bistable mechanical element with states 0 and 1 under force  F . The hysteron can be in state 1 for  F > F −  and state 0 for  F < F + . In the interval  F − < F < F +  the state depends on the history of the forcing. ( A ,  Center ) The state transition graph of four hysterons each coupling independently to the driving  F . ( A ,  Lower Right ) The ordering of the switching fields  F i ±  is as indicated. Black/gray (red/orange) arrows indicate state changes of the corresponding hysteron  i  when  F  is just above (below)  F i +  ( F i + ). A possible trajectory from 0000 to the state 0101 is shown by the black and red arrows. ( B ,  Top Left ) The experimental set up of ref.  2  for a crumpled sheet of paper driven by a variable strain Δ. ( B ,  Center ) The force–strain response under cyclic straining, once a periodic cycle has set in (yellow cycle). A subsequent driving protocol of the form shown in the lower right inset results in the subcycles shown. Adapted from Shohat et al. ( 2 ). The transition graph ( A ) and the cyclically sheared paper response ( B ) reveal a hierarchy of nested cycles characteristic of RPM.\\nConsider now a collection of  N  hysterons, each with a pair of threshold forces  F i ± , and each coupling independently to the applied force  F . One can construct a history-recording device by ordering the threshold forces as  F 1 + < F 2 + < … < F N +  and  F 1 − > F 2 − > … > F N − , as sketched in  Fig. 1 A ,  Lower Right . Initializing the device in a configuration where each hysteron is in its “0” state, upon increasing the force they will change states one by one in the order  1 , 2 , … , N . Due to the choice of ordering the  F i − , this will be also the same order in which the elements return from their “1” to their “0” state. A state transition graph of this system for the case  N  = 4 is shown in  Fig. 1 A . Here, gray/black (orange/red) arrows indicate transitions when the force has just increased (decreased) enough so that one element becomes unstable and changes state.\\nNote the nesting of cycles in  Fig. 1 A :  Starting from the state 0010, a sequence of gray/black arrows followed by orange/red arrows leads via 1110 back to 0010, forming a graph cycle, which in turn is nested within the cycle between states 0000 and 1110, etc. Observe also that from any state in the graph, by lowering the forcing sufficiently we can “reset” the system by bringing it back to the state 0000. The hierarchical nesting of cycles within cycles is a characteristic feature associated with return-point memory (RPM) ( 10 ), which emerges in the hysteretical magnetization response of magnets to an applied magnetic field. In the transition graph setting, the nesting feature is a topological property of the transitions between hysteron states, which is referred to as loop RPM ( 11 ). Assume now that starting in state 0000 a sequence of forcings leads the system to state 0101. The hierarchical nesting of cycles constrains the possible trajectories that the system must have followed in order to reach 0101 from the zero state: In particular, in the recent past the force must have risen above the value of  F 3 + , subsequently fallen, but not below  F 3 − , then risen again to a value between  F 2 +  and  F 3 + , etc. The shortest trajectory from 0000 to 0101 has been highlighted by the red and black arrows in  Fig. 1 A .\\nRemarkably, mechanical instabilities, which give rise to hysteresis in the form of near-perfect RPM with a hierarchy of nested hysteresis cycles, are rather ubiquitous. They are found in the athermal quasi-static response of various driven disordered systems, such as simulations of amorphous solids under shear strain ( 12 ) and experiments on sheared colloidal suspensions ( 13 ) as well as jammed granular particles under uniaxial compression ( 14 ). In all these systems thermal effects are negligible, and the mechanical instabilities are due to spatially localized plastic events, called soft spots ( 15 – 17 ), which effectively respond as hysterons. However, in contrast to the collection of noninteracting Preisach hysterons, these soft spots interact with each other via long-range elastic deformations. As a result, the state change of one soft spot can alter the switching fields of the other, but it can also give rise to new soft spots or deactivate existing ones by disabling their switching behavior. Overall, these interactions can give rise to highly complex dynamics, including avalanches where the instability of one soft spot triggers instabilities of multiple others, and more generally dynamically critical phenomena, such as yielding. The Preisach model, due to the absence of interactions, lacks all this complexity. Nevertheless, it is a conceptually simple model to illustrate key mechanisms of memory formation, such as RPM, serving a role similar to the ideal gas in statistical mechanics.\\nThe interactions between hysterons turn out to be both a blessing and a curse. They are a curse since in principle interactions can destroy the hierarchical RPM-type nesting of hysteresis cycles and hence adversely affect the capability of memory formation. They are a blessing since the interactions permit a degree of “programmability”: Cyclically driving the system until a periodic response has set in is tantamount to selecting a set of interacting soft spots that “play nice” with each other, i.e., they only moderately influence or impede each other’s switching behavior so that an RPM-like hierarchy of nested cycles remains largely intact.\\nSurprisingly, many of the driven disordered systems mentioned above achiev","next_offset":8500,"total_characters":13666,"raw_original":false}],"paging":"Large batches are paginated automatically; follow next_offset for remaining text.","tool_record_ref":"D8b1433930d15c503537f","tool_record_path":"/Applications/ideas/research/hysteron_deepseek_20261110/runtime/ours_source/runs/hypothesis_development_hysteron_generation/stages/02_initial_1_learn_0/api_v2/workspace/tools/f22659a8e8b9b218e69e409b81cb215f0b83f4862cde75a08d26aec47f354dee.json"}

messages.content: {"status":"read","documents":[{"ref":"D29f64daec76492b02eb4","sha256":"29f64daec76492b02eb411ed9602e6f0b9f174d4eab0f9772c0233d8d026503c","pointer":"/text","offset":8400,"text":" remains largely intact.\\nSurprisingly, many of the driven disordered systems mentioned above achieve both the programmability and nesting of hysteresis cycles, and the reasons for this are still not sufficiently understood. Now the paper by Shohat et al. ( 2 ) adds one more such system to the fray: a thin sheet of crumpled paper subject to driving via stretching and unstretching it ( Fig. 1 B ). The relation between the complex geometry of folds and creases of a crumpled sheet of paper and its mechanical response to external driving has so far been largely unexplored. By combining cyclic stretching protocols with three-dimensional (3D) imaging, Shohat et al. ( 2 ) are able to correlate the mechanical response of the sheet to its local geometrical transformation.\\nShohat et al. ( 2 ) find that when the sheet is cyclically strained it settles into a near-perfect periodic force–strain hysteresis cycle dotted with a large number of abrupt force jumps. Using 3D imaging, Shohat et al. ( 2 ) are able to trace the force jumps to localized plastic events in the sheet, originating from the snapping of vertices formed by the crossings of ridges ( 18 ). Shohat et al. ( 2 ) demonstrate that these mechanical instabilities behave as hysterons that interact with each other. As in the sheared amorphous solids, depending on the locations and states of the other hysterons, the interactions can facilitate or impede each other’s switching behavior. The sheet of paper has become a mechanical realization of a spin glass, an archetypical model for understanding the emergence of complexity in disordered systems ( 19 ).\\nThese findings set the stage for a thorough investigation of memory formation. First, Shohat et al. ( 2 ) “program” their sheet of paper by applying cyclic strain over a strain range  [ Δ 0 min , Δ 0 max ]  until a periodic response is attained in the force–strain response of the sheet ( Fig. 1 B ). The response to cyclic deformation has all the hallmarks of RPM. Once a periodic response has set in, a subsequent reduction of  Δ 0 max  to  Δ 1 max  results in force-versus-strain subcycles of the original hysteresis cycle, as depicted in  Fig. 1 B . In fact, the amplitude  Δ 1 max  can be lowered and raised as long as  Δ 1 max ≤ Δ 0 max , i.e., it does not exceed the value at which the original hysteresis cycle was obtained. Raising  Δ 1 max  back to  Δ 0 max , the original cycle is recovered. Thus, applying oscillatory shear to the crumpled paper has led to the selection of an interacting hysteron system that supports a hierarchy of cycles and subcycles, as shown in  Fig. 1 B . As in simulations of sheared amorphous solids ( 12 ), the emergence of the interacting hysteron system is at the heart of the memory that is imprinted into the disordered system as a result of cyclic loading. In fact, raising  Δ 1 max  to a value above  Δ 0 max  and then back to  Δ 0 max , Shohat et al. ( 2 ) show that this memory is erased.\\nThe relative ease with which the interacting hysterons of a driven disordered system establish a hierarchy of nested hysteresis cycles suggests that this may not have to be a consequence of the cyclic driving. The approximate rate independence of the response implies that the duration of the driving cycle is not important, while the hierarchy of nested cycles suggests that the driving need not be periodic, as long as it is confined to some range, e.g., the interval  [ Δ 0 min , Δ 0 max ]  in the case of the crumpled sheet. It is therefore conceivable that a random driving protocol confined to a range of values may produce a similar hierarchy of nested cycles and perhaps even enforce that the emerging set of soft spots “play nice.” If so, this implies that memory formation in athermal systems is more abundant in nature then one might have suspected, since the interactions of these systems with their fluctuating environment may suffice. One could thus regard these systems as simple and ad hoc sensors of their environment with the hysteron configurations serving as its representation. Seen in this way, the kitchen scale has a rather narrow representation of its environment in terms of the instantaneous displacement of its plate. On the other hand, a driven disordered system whose response to driving is capable of self-organizing into a hierarchy of nested hysteresis cycles establishes a complex representation of its environment and captures thereby certain features of the environment’s history.\\nWe tend to associate memory formation with elaborate processes of engineering design or long-term evolution. The work of Shohat et al. ( 2 ) provides a rather elegant and accessible table-top demonstration that this need not be the case. Memory formation in matter—at least in its most basic form—seems to be abundant, emerging rather easily. So, next time you crumple a piece of paper and throw it away, be aware. You may have created a memory.\\nM.M.’s work was funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) under Projektnummer 398962893, Projektnummer 21150405, and Projektnummer 390685813.\\nThe author declares no competing interest.\\nSee companion article, “Memory from coupled insta","next_offset":13600,"total_characters":13666,"raw_original":false}],"paging":"Large batches are paginated automatically; follow next_offset for remaining text.","tool_record_ref":"D9ff47225b4197c41d679","tool_record_path":"/Applications/ideas/research/hysteron_deepseek_20261110/runtime/ours_source/runs/hypothesis_development_hysteron_generation/stages/02_initial_1_learn_0/api_v2/workspace/tools/33786c5ea7cba5a10940e8c41207cf883be05d537f69359e0cf6ffefda4363f9.json"}

Excellent material. Key published points (Mungan commentary, PNAS 2022):
1. Preisach hysterons (independent coupling) with ordered thresholds ⇒ loop RPM (topological nesting).
2. Interactions: state change of one alters others' switching fields; can create/deactivate soft spots; avalanches where one instability triggers multiple others.
3. Interactions are "curse and blessing": can destroy RPM; also permit programmability. Cyclic driving selects interacting soft spots that "play nice" — "they only moderately influence or impede each other's switching behavior so that an RPM-like hierarchy of nested cycles remains largely intact."
4. Many driven disordered systems achieve both programmability and nesting; reasons not sufficiently understood.

This "play nice" is exactly a qualitative version of my Λ'/gap criterion. My contribution (conditional): replace "moderately influence" with a computable inequality on measured thresholds — "moderate" = coupling-induced threshold shift smaller than the drive gap to the partner's threshold (2|b_i| < gap), and note the crucial asymmetry: the relevant comparison is not |b| vs barrier h but |b| vs *threshold gap between partners*; a network of widely separated thresholds tolerates large coupling, while near-degenerate thresholds (as in network_C's coincident 5.8/5.8) cannot.

And importantly: RPM is *loop* RPM of the transition graph — a topological property. In network_C, I observe a single cycle repeated twice. Hmm: repeated identical cycle = periodic orbit; but RPM additionally requires nesting/subcycles on amplitude reduction. Since network_C was driven at constant amplitude, its repetition is consistent with any periodic orbit, not evidence for RPM. That's a sharpening: my branch 1 said "free-device event sequences generated by the table"; the published formal object is the state transition graph, and *what can be tested* is: does the graph's cycle structure nest? Only amplitude-reduction experiments would show it. So a conceptual consequence: network_C's 8-event cycle is at most a periodic orbit; RPM (nesting) is not testable from constant amplitude alone. This is a real, concrete correction to my earlier reading (I earlier called 逐字重复 "与 RPM 相容" — fine, but I should not treat it as evidence).

Also: "new soft spots can be created or deactivated" — this maps to my clamp_admissibility branch ("some clamped configurations may not exist in the free device"). In the published model, interactions can deactivate a hysteron entirely (it stops switching). That's exactly the "third state/missing event" phenomenon: interaction can disable switching. Good: my branch 4's mechanism (admissibility) has a published analogue — "interactions can give rise to new soft spots or deactivate existing ones by disabling their switching behavior." That supports treating "missing events" seriously rather than as measurement error, and gives the specific mechanism: if the interaction shift exceeds the width (2|b| > 2h), the hysteron becomes effectively monostable in that neighbor state → it never switches → "该翻而未翻". That's a crisp criterion: 2|b_i| ≥ 2h_i ⟺ Λ_i ≥ 1 ⟺ hysteron i is "disabled" (one of its two thresholds is pushed past the other, F^- > F^+ → no hysteresis, no switching). 

That resolves my open question "Λ=|b|/h 还是 Λ'=2|b|/阈值间隙?" — answer: BOTH, and they mean different things:
- Λ_i = |b_i|/h_i ≥ 1 ⟺ the hysteron is *disabled* (loses bistability, F^+ ≤ F^-) → missing events, no switching under that neighbor state.
- gap condition 2|b_i| ≥ |A_i − A_j| ⟺ *latch/double flip* (avalanche).
So the two dimensionless groups govern two different phenomena: disabling (admissibility) vs latching (ordering). This is a genuine conceptual clarification derived from combining the published statement (interactions can deactivate hysterons) with my decomposition (equal shift, fixed width). Beautiful. And check numbers: pair_A rotor2 at L=4.731: h=1.1, |b|=2.2 → Λ=2 ≥1 → rotor2 should be *disabled* (no hysteresis) when the neighbor is +1: F^+(σ=+1)=0.5, F^-(σ=+1)=−1.7 → still F^- < F^+ (0.5 > −1.7), width 2.2 >0. Hmm, so Λ=2|b|/2h = |b|/h = 2 >1 by my definition but F^- < F^+ still holds. Let me redo: width of the hysteresis window = F^+ − F^- = 2h = 2.2. The shift per neighbor-state change is Δ = 2b = −4.4 (for σ: −1→+1). Disabling occurs if the *shift* exceeds the window: |2b| > 2h ⟺ |b| > h ⟺ 2.2 > 1.1 ✓. But numerically F^+(+1)=0.5 > F^-(+1)=−1.7, so not disabled. Contradiction? Because disabling of the *relative* ordering: when the neighbor flips, i's threshold moves by 4.4, which is bigger than i's own window 2.2 → the state of i is not determined... Let's think about what "disabled" means: F^+ and F^- are both defined; the hysteron stays bistable as long as F^- < F^+ in every neighbor state. Here with σ=+1: 0.5 > −1.7, still bistable. So |b|>h does NOT disable. My equation above was wrong.

Disabling would need c to shift so much that F^+ < F^- : c changes; c(σ) = c0 + b σ, h fixed. F^+ = c + bσ + h, F^- = c + bσ − h. F^+ − F^- = 2h always >0 — so under pure equal shift, disabling is IMPOSSIBLE. Ah — that's an important consequence: the equal-shift/fixed-width form can never disable a hysteron; only a width change (h→0) can. So "deactivation of soft spots" in the published disordered-solid picture requires the interaction to change the *shape* (width/curvature), not just the field — a distinct piece of information!

That's a genuine conceptual consequence: the observed data (width invariant across neighbor states) implies that in this device interactions cannot deactivate hysterons; thus the "missing event" (该翻而未翻) in network_C cannot be explained by interaction-induced deactivation *if* the equal-shift/fixed-width form extends to the free device. Conversely, observing a permanently disabled rotor would refute the equal-shift form. This sharpens branch 4: admissibility is the only route to deactivation under my form; and the published mechanism ("new soft spots arise / existing deactivated") is exactly what the width-invariance forbids here. Great — that's a clean, testable distinction between my factorization and the general interacting-hysteron model, and a real intellectual consequence.

So: the two dimensionless groups:
- Latch (avalanche of size 2): 2|b_i| ≥ gap between partner thresholds (in the relevant state).
- Disabling (loss of switching): requires width change; under fixed width impossible.
So Λ=|b|/h is the wrong group for latching, and it also doesn't govern disabling under this form. That corrects my branch 3 which used Λ.

Now branch 3 (barrier_interaction_frontier): Λ_M = |b|/h monotone rising — I should revise: the actual design tension is (i) addressability = threshold gap, and (ii) coupling-driven collectivity. And h (barrier) enters only as the *width* that keeps RPM windows separated (the Preisach ordering requires F_i^- descending order). Hmm: with fixed width, large |b| doesn't destroy bistability, so the "barrier vs interaction" tension is weaker than I claimed. Revise: the trade-off is between threshold *spacing* (addressability, distinct drive levels) and coupling strength (collectivity/latching); the barrier width h is not the protective quantity. That's a substantive revision of branch 3's premise.

Now, does this weaken "barrier_interaction_frontier" to the point of parking? I'd revise it into a gap-based version, keeping the "one geometric knob controls both" idea: L increases |b| and shrinks w (hence shrinks gaps too, since all thresholds converge → 4.3/4.9 converge). Indeed at L=4.731 the two up thresholds are 5.5 and 4.9 (gap 0.6) vs at L=0: 7.3 and 3.5 (gap 3.8). So L shrinks the gap AND increases |b| → latch. Both factors push the same way: latch ⟺ 2|b| ≥ gap; L↑ ⇒ |b|↑ and gap↓ ⇒ crossing inevitable. That's the real "frontier" claim, much sharper than Λ. And it predicts a definite L* where 2|b_2(L)| = gap(L), with the observed transition between 3.154 (2|b|? let me check L=3.154: rotor2 up 5.9/... hmm I don't have full L=3.154 rotor2 rows. From prior stage: "转子2 的移动随 other_state 变号（other=−1 时 up 3.5→4.9，other=+1 时 3.5→0.5...)" only endpoints. My earlier claim "L=3.154 不满足（5.9>3.9）" suggests at L=3.154: rotor1 up with other=+1 = 5.9 and rotor2 up with other=−1 = 3.9? So gap 2.0, and 2|b_1| = ? rotor1 at L=3.154, other=−1 up 6.5, other=+1 5.9 → 2b_1 = −0.6 → |b|=0.3, 2|b|=0.6 < gap 2.0 → no latch. At L=4.731: 2|b_1|=1.2, gap = 5.5−4.9=0.6 → 1.2 ≥ 0.6 ✓ latch. So the crossing is between 3.154 and 4.731 for rotor1 latching on rotor2 — consistent with my earlier claim, now derived from the correct group. Good, and I can state it: at L=4.731 the gap-normalized group is 2|b_1|/gap = 1.2/0.6 = 2.0 > 1, while at L=3.154 it is 0.6/2.0 = 0.3 < 1.

Careful: rotor1's latch on rotor2 must compare rotor1's shift with the gap between rotor1's and rotor2's up thresholds. Yes: 2|b_1| = 1.2 vs gap 0.6.

That's a nice worked learning example.

Now also note: for rotor2 latching on rotor1: 2|b_2| = 4.4, gap = 0.6 → 7.3 ≫ 1 → also latches. Consistent (both directions in same state → same double flip).

Now, the crucial RPM point: a double flip preserves loop RPM? In the transition graph, a "double flip" (two hysterons flipping at the same field) is not part of the Preisach independent graph; it can create RPM violation or not. Known: ferro coupling → avalanches → and the graph can still show RPM (the disordered solid). So double flips per se don't destroy RPM. So my earlier implication "latch ⇒ RPM破坏" is wrong. And my criterion "Λ<1 keeps RPM" is wrong too. Revision: latching (double flips) is compatible with RPM; RPM violation requires *passing* (order inversions that make subcycles not nest), a property of the whole state-dependent threshold ordering, i.e., the "play nice" condition on the full graph. That is real content: I can now define the distinction:
- avalanche/latch: local, pairwise, computed from gaps; not an RPM criterion.
- RPM: global, topological property of the state-transition graph; needs the full ordered family of thresholds across all 2^N states.

Consequence: to predict network_C's cycle from pair data, one needs the 4-rotor additivity plus the full ordering; a 2-rotor table can only supply the pair-level matrix elements. And network_C's two coincidences (5.8/5.8, −5.1/−5.1) are consistent with avalanches but their directional structure (different partners in up vs down) is exactly what the state-dependent threshold model permits (partner identity depends on the state of all neighbors).

Good. Now let me also connect to the mechanical metamaterial "profusion" (three hysterons → >15,000 graphs, most violating RPM). Consequence: a 4-rotor device is in the regime where interaction-induced graph complexity explodes; observing a clean 8-event periodic cycle then is informative: it means the realized network sits in the "play nice" subset (as published: cyclic driving selects compatible sets). My device may have been iteratively tuned to exactly that (the brief says the apparatus was iteratively adjusted, non-random sampling) — so the clean cycle is partly a selection artifact. That's an important consideration (already a limitation).

Now, the personal question update: my current question was "在 pair_A 的夹紧阈值表里，耦合究竟改变了什么自由度——场 vs 势垒？两种改变对四转子网络的事件次序给出可区分后果吗?" This turn's answer: 场（等量平移），宽度不变 → 已在数据内确立; and the discriminating consequence is not about barrier but about two different thresholds: gap (latch) vs width (disable). 转子夹紧表决定。\"},\"reason\":\"只有分开这两种后果，我才能说出夹紧表能预测什么：它给的是逐对的阈值位移与间隙，可算锁存；但禁用需要宽度改变，而数据恰好显示宽度不变——这会把「缺失事件」的解释逼到另一条分支（位形不可实现）。这一区分直接改写我的分支内容与设计坐标。\",\"uptake\":[{\"consequence\":\"条件性后果：我的逐对不等式只应被读成「是否发生同 γ 1；设计上不存在同时保持「阈值清晰可分」与「强耦合集体响应」的中间区，只有沿这条线移动。\",\"base_version\":0,\"conceptual_move\":\"把设计张力从「势垒 vs 相互作用」（势垒在等量平移下并不承担保护作用）换成「地址可分性 vs 集体性」，并用 2|b|/间隙 作设计坐标；这同时解释了为什么「小回线/大位移阈值」能并存：宽度与间隙不是同一个量。\",\"depends_on\":[{\"key\":\"latch_as_threshold_inequality\",\"owner\":\"theory_scientist\",\"version\":1}],\"implications\":[\"条件性：为易切换而增大 L nice」（只适度影响彼此）不必是调参运气，而是间隙/耦合比的区间选择问题。\"],\"influenced_by\":[{\"key\":\"barrier_interaction_frontier\",\"owner\":\"theory_scientist\",\"version\":1}],\"key\":\"threshold_gap_addressability\",\"motivation\":\"pair_A：上翻阈值间隙从 ## 1. 本轮要解决的缺口

上一轮把「等量平移、宽度不变」同时当作两件事使用：(a) 同 γ 双翻（锁存）的来源，(b) 返回点记忆（RPM）的候选保护条件。缺口是：同一种「只改写切换场」的相互作用，到底产出哪一种后果；以及「某转子被停用/不再翻转」与「同 γ 双翻」是否只是同一判据的两个名字。

本轮请求的两个概念：等量平移形态下 hysteron 是否不可能被停用；「2|b| 对阈值间隙」是否就是 no-passing/dominance 判据的二元素特例。

## 3. 概念修正（本轮实际改变）

1. **删除「平移＋固定宽度可保护 RPM」这一用法。** 已发表：相互作用正是改写邻居切换场的形态，而三个相互作用 hysteron 已能生成 >15000 张转移图、多数破坏 RPM。逐对条件至多排除同 γ 双翻，不能保证 RPM。
2. **把「锁存」与「禁用」分成两个不同后果。** 在 F_i^± = c_i + b_ij σ_j ± h_i(L) 下，F^+ − F^− = 2h 与邻居态无关，故纯等量平移不可能停用 hysteron；要停用/新建软点必须有宽度（或更一般形状）改变。
3. **设计坐标从 |b|/h 改为 2|b|/相邻阈值间隙。**
4. **RPM 是整张状态转移图的嵌套拓扑性质**，不是「没有雪崩」的对偶；等幅循环的逐字重复只说明周期轨道，不构成 RPM 证据。

- L = 4.731 cm：A_1 = 5.5, A_2 = 4.9, b_1 = −0.6 → 2|b_1| = 1.2，间隙 = 0.6；比值 2.0 ≥ 1 → 预言 4.9 cm 处同 γ 双翻。

两个因子（|b| 上升、间隙缩小）同向，故转变点落在已测区间 (3.154, 4.731) 之间，只能给区间，不能给数值。此计算是条件性的：前提是可加形式与「b 可由夹紧态迁移到自由态」，两者均未检验。

- 「软点新建」在阈值坐标里对应什么（h 变负？新增维度？）不清楚。
- 多邻居线性可加在自由装置是否成立未知；3 个以上相互作用 hysteron 的转移图已呈爆炸式复杂。
- case 事实仍为 unknown：mount_l_cm 的端点语义；network_C 的连通性、停位角、驱动振幅与反转点。

{"draft_ref": "D06a551b9b448d78add42", "edits": [{"op": "set", "path": "/files", "value": {"learning_note_02_initial_1_learn_0.md": "# 学习笔记：相互作用 hysteron、锁存与 RPM 的层级（02_initial_1_learn_0）

## 1. 本轮要修的缺口
上一轮我把「等量平移两阈值、宽度不变」同时当作两件事使用：(a) 同 γ 双翻（锁存）的来源；(b) return-point memory（RPM）的候选保护条件。需要判定同一个「平移」到底产出哪一种后果，以及「某转子被禁用/不再翻转」与「同 γ 双翻」是否只是同一判据的两个名字。

## 2. 已发表知识（非我的发现）
- 三个相互作用 hysteron 可生成 >15000 张状态转移图，其中多数破坏 RPM；而由独立 Preisach 单元出发的通路总满足 RPM（K178eb3527f39324a，摘要级）。
- RPM 是 hysteron 态之间转移的**嵌套性质**，是整张转移图的拓扑性质（Kd215cb6fc530a930，摘要级；K3cf0891db02054d4 全文讨论段）。
- 相互作用可以改写邻居的切换场，并可「新建软点或停用已有软点」（K3cf0891db02054d4 全文；S10 摘录）。
- 矢量 hysteron/PSW 摘要只说相互作用场使回线中心位移、临界面穿越时核对能量损失——支持「平移中心而不改宽度」的术语，但无判据、无 RPM 讨论（Kf9ece236650c0966）。
- 串联机械 hysteron 的耦合符号可由几何控制（反铁磁式），可用于设计通路并破坏 RPM（Kef1bd787ff0ba494，摘要）。
- 波纹板压缩把通路按相互作用强度分为 Preisach／scrambled／accumulator 三类，给出「随耦合增强通路类别改变」的定性谱系（K167248283ece360c，摘要）。
- 相互作用被建模为对单个翻转应变的随机或固定位移，并讨论 Preisach RPM（K3c2b6ea13200cfe4，全文）。

## 3. 我的推论（明确标为推论，未经检验）
- 因为 F⁺−F⁻ = 2h 与邻居态 σ_j 无关，纯等量平移**不可能**禁用某转子的双稳性；禁用/新建必然对应宽度（形状）改变。这是代数推论，尚未与已发表的停用/no-passing 条件逐条对照。
- 锁存判据因此改用间隙归一化：2|b_i| ≥ (A_i − A_j)，即在 pair_A 中 L=3.154 cm 比值为 0.23、L=4.731 cm 为 2.0，转变落在已测区间 (3.154, 4.731) 内（学习性条件推演，非验证）。
- 上一版的 Λ=|b|/h 混用了两种现象（排序 vs 存在性），故不再作为设计坐标。
- 等量平移本身不是 RPM 的保护条件：它正是制造雪崩与记忆失效的标准形态，因此「易切换」与「保 RPM」不能由同一逐对不等式给出。

## 4. 未决 / 保留的分支
- 「等量平移 ⇒ 不可停用」未与原文停用条件对照（本轮检索未取到原始文献）。
- 多邻居线性可加在自由装置是否成立未知；3 个以上相互作用 hysteron 的转移图已呈爆炸式复杂。
- network_C 的并列对（升段 s1/s3、降段 s1/s2）与「状态依赖的伙伴身份」相容，也与「偶然近简并」相容；记录约定只保证顺序、不保证时间间隔，故仍不判定。
- 两项案例事实仍为 unknown：mount_l_cm 指哪一端臂；network_C 的驱动振幅/反转点。
- 「共用 w(L)」这一观测仍无机制解释。

## 5. 分类为无关的来源（保留以便追溯）
MSMA 执行器的 Preisach/play 建模与逆补偿（Ka9e811033696759a）、压电陶瓷/SMA 的 Preisach 建模摘要（Ke85fd9d7c2fe7cbc）、经典 Preisach 算子的测度表示与可逆性（K5ab4a5f8e64414c5）、以及串联机械 hysteron 的重复条目（K690a760e178df473）。

In peer discussion, engage a specific assumption: elaborate a consequence, expose a hidden
premise, connect a disciplinary concept, propose a distinct explanation, or revise a relation.
Explain the reasoning. You may retain, revise, branch, or park your own line. No forced consensus,
disagreement, novelty claim, completed hypothesis or compulsory new branch each turn.
Evidence strength, proof, available data/tools, implementation and experimental feasibility
are NOT requirements for proposing, retaining or prioritizing a hypothesis. Do not turn
discussion into a feasibility review. Research/analysis requests remain optional resources
for thinking. Correct concrete errors in premises while keeping conditional hypotheses distinct
from established observations; lack of evidence alone is not a refutation.

hypothesis_state.self contains your saved branches; peer_branches belong to their named owners.
Return hypothesis_updates: [] when nothing changed, otherwise full cards:
{key: stable local identifier [A-Za-z0-9_]+, base_version: 0 for new or supplied own version,
assumption: nonempty provisional claim, motivation: specific phenomenon/difficulty/relation,
conceptual_move: string or null if still unclear,
implications: [specific conditional consequences, may be empty],
open_questions: [unresolved conceptual questions, may be empty],
status: developing/parked, reason: why propose/change/park/resume,
influenced_by: [exact ref objects from supplied hypothesis_state],
depends_on: [exact supplied hypothesis refs used as premises; [] if none]}.
Influence is not logical dependence. Declare depends_on only for actual premises; do not invent
links. revision_obligations lists your branches whose declared premises changed or themselves
await review. This does NOT mean the branch is false. For each obligation return
 dependency_responses:[{ref:exact hypothesis_ref,action:revise/reaffirm/park/unresolved,reason}].
Reaffirm/revise requires an updated full card citing current dependency versions; changing only
links is recorded as provenance maintenance, not conceptual progress. Park/unresolved retains
the branch and its warning. Reasoned reaffirmation is valid; do not mechanically follow criticism.
Dependencies not explicitly declared cannot be inferred by this structural checker.
Omitting a branch retains it. To keep an alternative, use a new key and cite the parent ref;
never overwrite a peer's branch. Missing conceptual_move or implications is allowed for an
early assumption. Keep hypothetical consequences explicitly hypothetical, including examples.
Reusable conceptual learning can also be saved through existing memory_notes, kind:hypothesis,
with actual source provenance and same-key revisions. Run-local branches do not replace your
long-term disciplinary memory or its source screening. Do not invent empirical support.


Optional learning_request: {needed:boolean, gap, why_now, queries:[strings],
urls:[], source_ids:[], record_ids:[], operations:[], case_questions:[]}.
Use case_questions for actual case definitions/units/processing order; literature cannot
reconstruct undocumented case facts. These questions dispatch even when needed:false.
General theory and explanation-development requests use queries/gap. For case facts, the
isolated material service releases supported neutral definitions, not hidden conclusions.
The controller searches and returns actual readable content. Keep your own scientific query;
classify returned sources as directly relevant, transferable method, or irrelevant, with reasons.
Do not treat a successful download as understanding. No compulsory tool use.
For a small worked calculation use an operation {kind:"calculation", question,
bindings:{name: numeric scalar/array}, expression: numeric array expression,
expected: optional numeric value/array}. Available arithmetic, slices and named functions
include mean,sum,std,norm,diff,abs,sqrt. Define which rows/columns mean which entities.
Top-level analysis_plan also dispatches. needed:false disables literature search, not explicit
calculations. Unsupported requests return a pending capability task; no scientific rejection.
Keep purely tentative proposals in hypothesis_updates/next_actions, not execution fields.


HYPOTHESIS CONTENT CYCLE:
Use development_cycle as a thinking context, not a demand to invent progress. Choose one
specific explanatory relation, construction, distinction or unresolved phenomenon from its
sources. Locate the conceptual gap: what connection/premise/consequence is still unclear?
Choose a next move because of this gap: learn, derive, connect, reframe, or hold. Explain why
that move could change understanding. For learning, use this gap in learning_request.gap and
why_now, and formulate targeted queries; do not request a broad survey merely to fill a stage.
In discussion, take up a peer's concrete relation and explain how your discipline extends,
challenges or changes its consequences. Generic agreement about controls or feasibility is
not a substitute; a measurement contribution is valid when its specific consequences matter.
Study returned services against the gap that requested them, including failures and pending
capabilities. Do not call retrieval success learning. If nothing changes, say so and preserve
the gap. Own previous_steps carry unfinished thinking across phases and sessions. When the
controller flags repeated_no_change, reconsider the missing connection, premise, or next
learning move; holding a branch is valid. The flag uses supplied peer content comparisons, not a quality verdict. A shared interpretation is normal.
Return development_step:{focus:{source:exact development_cycle.sources key,quote:exact excerpt},
gap:nonempty text, action:learn/derive/connect/reframe/hold, reason:nonempty text,
expected_change:text or null for hold,
uptake:[{source:exact source key,quote:exact excerpt or null only for unresolved,
effect:revise/extend/challenge/unchanged/unresolved,reason:how this affects the focus,
consequence:conditional consequence or null when none follows}],
outcome:{kind:relation/implication/clarification/unchanged/uncertain,
statement:what changed or did not, remaining_gap:text or null}}.
Account once for EACH service key in required_service_uptake. If peer_sources is nonempty,
engage at least one (unresolved with a reason is valid). Other uptake is optional. Quotes must
come from the named source; for published claims quote readable source content, not metadata.
For relation/implication outcomes, preserve the resulting claim in a hypothesis_update's
assumption or implications. This records an author's proposal, NOT confirmed novelty/progress.
No compulsory new relation, branch, agreement, data, experiment, proof or implementation.


QUESTION STATE PROTOCOL v2:
question_state.self is YOUR authoritative current personal question. peer_questions belong
to their named owners. shared_question is the discussion's current shared question, or null.
Do not reconstruct your prior question from the latest peer message. The controller records
the actual before-state; do NOT return question_before or question_after.
Return personal_question_update: {base: the exact self.ref object, action: retain/revise,
question: your current or revised personal question, reason: a nonempty explanation,
influenced_by: array of exact question ref objects from this supplied packet}.
Retain means the question text stays exactly the same. Revise may include adopting a peer's
line or the shared question: explain why; use influenced_by to identify relevant question refs.
You need not preserve disagreement or a distinct personal question if you decide to change it.
Separately return shared_question_update: null, or {base: the exact shared_question.ref (null
if none yet), action: propose/revise/retain, question: shared question text, reason: nonempty,
influenced_by: array of refs from this packet}. Propose is only for a first shared question.
A shared question is a versioned proposal, not proof of peer agreement. Revising it NEVER
changes another researcher's personal question. Your own personal update is independent too.

Use controller-owned question_state, never invent question_before/question_after.
Keep hypotheses tied to specific entities/relations in this situation. A measurement or representation contribution is legitimate; explain its concrete consequences without forcing a natural mechanism.
